# dsh-browser

DSH plugin: an isolated Playwright browser per session — live tab thumbnails in the composer dock,
a

**Browser** section in the sidebar, a per-site proxy and DevTools-grade tooling for agents.
16 tool

s, 33 `browser_run` commands (including `list`/`help` and the network presets), a settings
form, and
a regression suite.

Real Chromium (Playwright) for every DSH session: live thumbnails in the dock, a **Browser**
section
in the sidebar, a per-site proxy and full DevTools access.

## What it gives

- **A browser per agent.** A separate process, a separate temporary profile, its own tabs.
A subagen

t gets its own browser and cannot see anyone else's.
- **Contexts.** `ctx1`, `ctx2`, … — isolated co

okies and storage inside one browser,
so two clients can be tested against one server.
- **Live fram

es.** The dock card shows tab thumbnails and a virtual pointer;
after actions (`open`, `navigate`, `

click`, `resize`, `drag`) a frame is posted to the chat.
- **Browser section in the sidebar.** A lis

t of open browsers grouped by session:
session name, number of tabs, jumping to the session, closing

an individual browser.
- **Per-site proxy.** A built-in routing proxy on `127.0.0.1:49222`: it look

s at the host
of every connection and routes only the listed sites through Hiddify, everything else

goes direct.
Chromium 156 ignores PAC (both `--proxy-pac-url` and `chrome.proxy` from an extension),

so the
decision is made outside the browser. The site list and the proxy address persist across res

tarts
in the data directory: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dsh-browser` (Windows), `~/.local/share/dsh-browser` (L

inux),
`~/Library/Application Support/dsh-browser` (macOS).
- **Debugging.** Network, console, cooki
es, storage, IndexedDB, coverage, accessibility snapshot, Lighthouse.
## Tools
| Tool | Purpose |

| `browser_open` | open a tab (optionally in a specific `ctx`) |
| `browser_navigate` | navigate to

a URL |
| `browser_click` | click a CSS selector (not blocked by a dialog) |
| `browser_fill` | fill

a field |
| `browser_hover` / `browser_drag` | pointer and drag (within the viewport) |
| `browser_

resize` | viewport size |
| `browser_text` | page text |
| `browser_tabs` | tab list |
| `browser_cl

ose` | close a tab (the last one shuts the browser down) |
| `browser_cdp` | raw Chrome DevTools Pro

tocol call |
| `browser_run` | command dispatcher (see below) |
| `browser_proxy_enable` / `browser_
proxy_disable` / `browser_proxy_status` / `browser_proxy_list` | proxy |
All tools accept `timeout` (ms). The default is 10–45 s depending on the operation.
## `browser_run` commands
`browser_run({ command: "list" })` — the catalogue; `{ command: "help", args: { name: "network" } }`
n({ command: "list" })` — the catalogue; `{ command: "help", args: { name: "network" } }` — details.
| Command | What it does |

| `console` | `console.*` and page errors, including asynchronous ones |
| `network` | requests with

codes, types and errors |
| `cookies` | get / set / clear |
| `storage` | `localStorage` / `session

Storage` |
| `idb` | IndexedDB: databases, stores, rows |
| `eval` | run JS, return the value |
| `d

om` | html / text / attrs / styles / count of an element |
| `snapshot` | accessibility tree (role a

nd name) |
| `keyboard` | `press`, `type`, `down`, `up` |
| `dialog` | `accept` / `dismiss` / text f

or `prompt` |
| `emulate` | network, color scheme, CPU, time zone, geolocation |
| `metrics` | page

performance metrics |
| `perf` | record the main thread for N seconds: where the time went |
| `slow

3g` / `fast3g` / `offline` / `off` | network presets in one word |
| `trace` | record a Playwright t

race |
| `coverage` | JS coverage between start and stop |
| `downloads` | files downloaded by the b

rowser |
| `lighthouse` | audit: scores, metrics, failed checks |
| `report` | parse a saved report:

list or a single audit |
| `css` | matched rules for an element: selectors, properties, media queri

es, fonts |
| `assets` | page resources by type, `download: true` — save to disk |
| `html` | the fu

ll document HTML into a file |
| `screenshot` | page or element snapshot into a file (opened with `r

ead_image`) |
| `diff` | pixel comparison of two screenshots |
| `ws` | WebSocket connections and fr

ames in both directions |
| `wait` | wait for a selector or text |
| `ctx` | tabs by context |
| `cd
p` | an arbitrary protocol method |
## Architecture

- **Host** (`index.js`) keeps one manager per agent, registers the tools and the `127.0.0.1:49221`
b

ridge for the client part.
- **Manager** (`src/browser-manager.js`) launches Chromium through `launc

hPersistentContext`
in a temporary profile that is deleted when the browser closes.
- **Bridge** (`s

rc/bridge.js`) serves tabs, frames and proxy state to the client.
- **Client** (`client.js`) draws t

he dock card, the sidebar section and the tool-row view
with a frame thumbnail.
- **Proxy** (`src/ro
uting-proxy.js`) routes connections according to rules from the bridge.
## Limitations

- **`lighthouse`** requires the package to be installed; without it the command returns a clear
erro
r and the rest of the plugin keeps working.
## Requirements

- Chromium from Playwright (`ms-playwright`); the path can be set via `DSH_BROWSER_EXE`.
- `lighthou

se` — an optional dependency: the `lighthouse` command returns a clear error
if the package is not i
nstalled. The rest of the plugin works without it.
